questions.question: A particle starts from rest. Its acceleration at time t seconds is a = 2t m/s². The distance travelled in the first 3 s is
questions.explanation: Acceleration a = dv/dt = 2t. Integrating from rest, v = t². Distance s = ∫ v dt = ∫ t² dt from 0 to 3 = [t³/3] from 0 to 3 = 9 m.

questions.question: A particle is projected from level ground with speed 20 m/s. Take g = 10 m/s². The maximum possible horizontal range, in metres, is
questions.explanation: Range R = u² sin 2θ / g. This is maximum when sin 2θ = 1, so 2θ = 90° and θ = 45°. Rmax = u²/g = 400/10 = 40 m.

questions.question: A car starts from rest and reaches 20 m/s in 10 s at constant acceleration. It then moves at 20 m/s for the next 10 s. It finally comes to rest in the next 5 s at constant deceleration. The total distance travelled, in metres, is
questions.explanation: Stage 1: average speed 10 m/s for 10 s, so s1 = 100 m. Stage 2: s2 = 20 × 10 = 200 m. Stage 3: average speed 10 m/s for 5 s, so s3 = 50 m. Total s = 100 + 200 + 50 = 350 m.

questions.question: A man walks due east at 3 m/s. To him, rain appears to fall vertically. The actual velocity of the rain makes 30° with the vertical. The speed of the rain is
questions.explanation: Rain appears vertical, so the horizontal component of the rain velocity equals the man's speed, 3 m/s east. If the actual rain velocity makes 30° with the vertical, its horizontal component is v sin 30° = v/2. Thus v/2 = 3, so v = 6 m/s.

questions.question: A ball is thrown vertically upward with speed 20 m/s. Take g = 10 m/s². The total distance travelled by the ball until it returns to the point of projection is
questions.explanation: Maximum height H = u²/(2g) = 400/20 = 20 m. The ball goes up 20 m and comes down 20 m, so the path length is 40 m. The displacement for the round trip is zero, but distance is not.

chapter: Laws of Motion and Work, Power, Energy
subject: physics

questions.question: Two masses of 3 kg and 1 kg hang from a light inextensible string over a frictionless pulley. Take g = 10 m/s². The magnitude of acceleration of either mass, in m/s², is
questions.explanation: For an Atwood machine, a = (m1 − m2)g / (m1 + m2) = (3 − 1) × 10 / (3 + 1) = 20/4 = 5 m/s². The heavier mass descends.

questions.question: A spring of force constant 100 N/m is compressed by 20 cm on a smooth horizontal table and a 1 kg block is released from rest against it. The maximum speed of the block is
questions.explanation: Spring energy converts fully into kinetic energy: (1/2)kx² = (1/2)mv². So v = x √(k/m) = 0.20 × √(100/1) = 0.20 × 10 = 2 m/s.

questions.question: A 5 kg block is on a horizontal surface with coefficient of kinetic friction 0.2. A horizontal force of 20 N is applied. Take g = 10 m/s². The acceleration of the block, in m/s², is
questions.explanation: Normal reaction N = mg = 50 N. Kinetic friction f = μN = 0.2 × 50 = 10 N, opposite the motion. Net force = 20 − 10 = 10 N. a = 10/5 = 2 m/s². The applied force exceeds limiting friction, so the block does slide.

questions.question: A 2 kg body on a smooth horizontal surface is accelerated from rest to 4 m/s by a horizontal force. The work done by that force is
questions.explanation: By the work-energy theorem, work done by the only horizontal force equals the gain in kinetic energy. ΔK = (1/2)mv² − 0 = (1/2)(2)(16) = 16 J.

questions.question: A bullet of mass 0.01 kg moving at 200 m/s embeds in a stationary block of mass 1.99 kg. The kinetic energy converted into heat and deformation, in joules, is
A solid sphere and a thin spherical shell have the same mass and radius and roll without slipping down the same incline from rest. The ratio of their linear accelerations (solid sphere : shell) is
questions.explanation: For rolling without slipping, a = g sinθ / (1 + I/(MR²)). For a solid sphere I/(MR²) = 2/5, so a_s = g sinθ / (7/5) = (5/7) g sinθ. For a thin spherical shell I/(MR²) = 2/3, so a_h = g sinθ / (5/3) = (3/5) g sinθ. Ratio a_s/a_h = (5/7) ÷ (3/5) = 25/21.

questions.question: A uniform disc of mass 2 kg and radius 0.4 m rotates at 10 rad/s about its central axis perpendicular to its plane. Its rotational kinetic energy, in joules, is
questions.explanation: For a disc about its central axis, I = (1/2)MR² = (1/2)(2)(0.4)² = 0.16 kg m². Rotational KE = (1/2)Iω² = (1/2)(0.16)(100) = 8 J.

questions.question: The moment of inertia of a thin ring of mass M and radius R about a diameter is
questions.explanation: About the axis through the centre and perpendicular to the plane, I_z = MR². That axis and two perpendicular diameters are mutually perpendicular. By the perpendicular-axis theorem, I_z = I_x + I_y. Symmetry gives I_x = I_y, so each diameter has I = MR²/2.

questions.question: A particle of mass 2 kg moves at 3 m/s. The perpendicular distance from a fixed axis to its velocity line is 4 m. The magnitude of its angular momentum about that axis, in kg m²/s, is
questions.explanation: For a particle, L = m v r_perp when v is perpendicular to the position arm used, or more generally L = m v d where d is the perpendicular distance from the axis to the line of velocity. L = 2 × 3 × 4 = 24 kg m²/s.

questions.question: A solid cylinder of mass 4 kg rolls without slipping on a horizontal surface at centre-of-mass speed 2 m/s. Its total kinetic energy, in joules, is
questions.explanation: Total KE = translational + rotational = (1/2)mv² + (1/2)Iω². For a solid cylinder I = (1/2)mR² and ω = v/R, so rotational KE = (1/4)mv². Total KE = (3/4)mv² = (3/4)(4)(4) = 12 J.

chapter: Gravitation and Mechanical Properties of Solids and Fluids
subject: physics

questions.question: The acceleration due to gravity at a height equal to the Earth's radius R, above the surface, is
questions.explanation: Outside the Earth, g(h) = GM/(R+h)². At h = R, g' = GM/(2R)² = (GM/R²)/4 = g/4. The linear approximation g(1 − 2h/R) is only for h much smaller than R, so it must not be used here.

questions.question: For a planet, the ratio of escape speed from the surface to the orbital speed of a satellite in a very low circular orbit is
questions.explanation: Orbital speed near the surface is v_o = √(GM/R) = √(gR). Escape speed is v_e = √(2GM/R) = √(2gR). Therefore v_e / v_o = √2.

questions.question: A large open tank is filled with water. A small hole is opened 5 m below the free surface. Take g = 10 m/s² and neglect viscosity. The speed of efflux, in m/s, is
questions.explanation: Torricelli's result from Bernoulli's equation, comparing the free surface (speed nearly zero, pressure atmospheric) with the hole (pressure atmospheric), gives v = √(2gh) = √(2 × 10 × 5) = √100 = 10 m/s.

questions.question: In a hydraulic lift the area of the output piston is 10 times the area of the input piston. A force of 50 N on the input piston supports a load on the output piston of how many newtons? Neglect the weight of the pistons.
questions.explanation: Pascal's law: pressure is transmitted undiminished, so F1/A1 = F2/A2. Thus F2 = F1 (A2/A1) = 50 × 10 = 500 N.

questions.question: A Carnot engine operates between 600 K and 300 K. Its efficiency is
questions.explanation: Carnot efficiency η = 1 − T_cold/T_hot = 1 − 300/600 = 1/2 = 50%. Temperatures must be in kelvin, which they already are. No real engine between the same temperatures can exceed this.

questions.question: The number of degrees of freedom of a diatomic ideal gas at room temperature, when vibrational modes are not excited, is
questions.explanation: A diatomic molecule has 3 translational degrees of freedom and 2 rotational degrees of freedom. At room temperature the vibrational mode of gases such as O2 and N2 is frozen, so f = 3 + 2 = 5. Then Cv = fR/2 = 5R/2 and γ = 1 + 2/f = 7/5.

questions.question: For a fixed amount of ideal gas taken through an isothermal process, the change in internal energy is
questions.explanation: For an ideal gas, internal energy depends only on temperature (and the amount of gas). In an isothermal process ΔT = 0, so ΔU = 0. The heat absorbed equals the work done by the gas, nRT ln(V2/V1), but that is Q, not ΔU.

questions.question: The adiabatic index γ = Cp/Cv for a monatomic ideal gas is
questions.explanation: A monatomic gas has f = 3. Cv = fR/2 = 3R/2 and Cp = Cv + R = 5R/2. Therefore γ = Cp/Cv = (5R/2)/(3R/2) = 5/3. The value 7/5 belongs to a diatomic gas with f = 5.

questions.question: Charges +q and −q are placed a distance 2a apart. The electric potential at the midpoint of the line joining them is
questions.explanation: The midpoint is at distance a from each charge. Potential is a scalar: V = kq/a + k(−q)/a = 0. The electric field there is not zero; the two fields point in the same direction and add. Do not confuse field with potential.

questions.question: Two capacitors of 6 μF each are connected in series. Their equivalent capacitance, in μF, is
questions.explanation: For series capacitors, 1/C = 1/C1 + 1/C2 = 1/6 + 1/6 = 1/3. Hence C = 3 μF. Series combination reduces capacitance; the parallel value would have been 12 μF.

questions.question: A capacitor of capacitance 2 μF is charged to 10 V. The energy stored, in microjoules, is
A 12 V battery is connected to a 2 Ω resistor in series with a parallel combination of two 4 Ω resistors. The current drawn from the battery, in amperes, is

questions.explanation: The two 4 Ω resistors are in parallel, so 1/Rp = 1/4 + 1/4 and Rp = 2 Ω. This is in series with 2 Ω, so Rtotal = 2 + 2 = 4 Ω. Current I = V/R = 12/4 = 3 A.

questions.question: In a balanced Wheatstone bridge, P = 2 Ω, Q = 4 Ω and R = 3 Ω. The fourth resistance S, in ohms, is
questions.explanation: The balance condition is P/Q = R/S. So 2/4 = 3/S, which means 1/2 = 3/S, hence S = 6 Ω. At balance, the galvanometer branch carries no current.

questions.question: A straight wire of length 0.4 m carries a current of 5 A perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of 0.5 T. The magnitude of the force on the wire, in newtons, is
questions.explanation: F = I l B sinθ. Here θ = 90°, so sinθ = 1. F = 5 × 0.4 × 0.5 = 1 N. The direction is given by the right-hand rule and is perpendicular to both the current and the field.

questions.question: A conducting rod of length 2 m moves at 5 m/s perpendicular to its length and perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of 0.2 T. The induced emf across the rod, in volts, is
questions.explanation: Motional emf = B l v when B, l and v are mutually perpendicular. emf = 0.2 × 2 × 5 = 2 V. The charges in the rod experience a magnetic force until the electric field balances it.

questions.question: A charged particle moves perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field. Its time period does not depend on
questions.explanation: The cyclotron period is T = 2πm/(qB). Speed and radius cancel because a faster particle moves on a larger circle, r = mv/(qB), and the extra path is exactly compensated. T depends on m, q and B, but not on speed.

questions.question: A series circuit has R = 3 Ω and inductive reactance XL = 4 Ω, with no capacitor. The rms supply voltage is 10 V. The rms current, in amperes, is
questions.explanation: Impedance Z = √(R² + XL²) = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5 Ω. Irms = Vrms/Z = 10/5 = 2 A. The power factor is R/Z = 3/5, but the question asks only for current.

questions.question: An ideal transformer has 100 turns in the primary and 500 turns in the secondary. The primary voltage is 220 V. The secondary voltage, in volts, is
questions.explanation: For an ideal transformer, Vs/Vp = Ns/Np. Vs = 220 × (500/100) = 220 × 5 = 1100 V. This is a step-up transformer. Current steps down in the same ratio so that input power equals output power.

questions.question: An object is placed 30 cm to the left of a thin convex lens of focal length 10 cm. Using the sign convention that distances to the left of the lens are negative, the image distance v, in cm, is
questions.explanation: Lens formula: 1/v − 1/u = 1/f. Here u = −30 cm and f = +10 cm. 1/v = 1/f + 1/u = 1/10 + 1/(−30) = 1/10 − 1/30 = 1/15. So v = +15 cm. The positive sign means a real image 15 cm to the right of the lens.

questions.question: An object is placed at the centre of curvature of a concave mirror of focal length 15 cm. The magnitude of the image distance, in cm, is
questions.explanation: New Cartesian sign convention: f = −15 cm and the centre of curvature is at u = −30 cm. Mirror formula: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f. 1/v = 1/f − 1/u = −1/15 − 1/(−30) = −1/15 + 1/30 = −1/30. So v = −30 cm. The magnitude is 30 cm. The image is real, inverted, and the same size.

questions.question: In Young's double-slit experiment, λ = 500 nm, the slit separation is 0.5 mm and the screen is 1 m away. The fringe width, in millimetres, is
questions.imageUrl: data:image/svg+xml;utf8,<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 420 200'><rect width='420' height='200' fill='%231E1E1E'/><text x='16' y='24' fill='%23F3ECDF' font-size='14' font-family='sans-serif'>Double slit: d = 0.5 mm, D = 1 m, λ = 500 nm</text><line x1='70' y1='40' x2='70' y2='170' stroke='%23F3ECDF' stroke-width='3'/><circle cx='70' cy='90' r='5' fill='%23E4A23A'/><circle cx='70' cy='120' r='5' fill='%23E4A23A'/><text x='82' y='86' fill='%23F3ECDF' font-size='13' font-family='sans-serif'>S1</text><text x='82' y='128' fill='%23F3ECDF' font-size='13' font-family='sans-serif'>S2</text><line x1='70' y1='90' x2='340' y2='70' stroke='%23E4A23A' stroke-width='1.5'/><line x1='70' y1='120' x2='340' y2='70' stroke='%23A39886' stroke-width='1.5'/><line x1='340' y1='40' x2='340' y2='170' stroke='%23F3ECDF' stroke-width='3'/><text x='300' y='190' fill='%23F3ECDF' font-size='13' font-family='sans-serif'>screen</text><text x='150' y='160' fill='%23A39886' font-size='13' font-family='sans-serif'>D = 1 m</text></svg>
questions.explanation: Fringe width β = λD/d. Convert units: λ = 5 × 10⁻⁷ m, d = 0.5 × 10⁻³ m = 5 × 10⁻⁴ m, D = 1 m. β = (5 × 10⁻⁷)(1)/(5 × 10⁻⁴) = 10⁻³ m = 1 mm.

questions.question: A ray in glass of refractive index √2 is incident on a plane glass-air surface. The critical angle, in degrees, is
questions.explanation: For glass to air, sin C = 1/μ = 1/√2. Therefore C = 45°. If the angle of incidence in glass exceeds 45°, the ray is totally reflected.

questions.question: A thin prism of angle 4° is made of a material of refractive index 1.5. The angle of minimum deviation, in degrees, is
questions.explanation: For a thin prism, δ_m = (μ − 1)A = (1.5 − 1) × 4° = 0.5 × 4° = 2°. This small-angle result is the one used in JEE when A is only a few degrees.

questions.question: Light of wavelength 310 nm falls on a metal of work function 2.0 eV. Take hc = 1240 eV·nm. The maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons, in eV, is
questions.explanation: Photon energy E = hc/λ = 1240/310 = 4.0 eV. Einstein's equation: Kmax = E − φ = 4.0 − 2.0 = 2.0 eV. The stopping potential would be 2.0 V.

questions.question: The wavelength, in nanometres, of a photon of energy 2.00 eV is (take hc = 1240 eV·nm)
questions.explanation: E = hc/λ, so λ = hc/E = 1240/2.00 = 620 nm. This is in the visible red region.

questions.question: In the Bohr model of hydrogen, the ratio of the radius of the n = 2 orbit to the radius of the n = 1 orbit is
questions.explanation: Bohr radius of the nth orbit is r_n = n² a0. Therefore r2/r1 = (2)² / (1)² = 4. The speed in that orbit is half the ground-state speed, and the energy is −13.6/4 = −3.4 eV.

questions.question: The half-life of a radioactive sample is 3 hours. The time, in hours, after which its activity falls to 1/16 of the initial activity is
questions.explanation: Activity is proportional to the number of undecayed nuclei. A/A0 = (1/2)^n = 1/16, so n = 4 half-lives. Time t = 4 × 3 = 12 hours.
